slides.title:
IMSDA Events
Getting started
slides.say: IMSDA Events is our shared place for club records and event participation. Today we will follow the tasks you are most likely to need: signing in, keeping a club's information up to date, registering for an event and reviewing clubs as a coordinator. You do not need to understand the software behind it. Start with your own account and the job you are doing.
slides.show: Open events.imsda.org. For demonstrations, use an approved training account and fictitious records. The step illustrations in this deck are teaching aids, not screenshots or proposed menus.

slides.title: Why we use IMSDA Events
cards: Keep club information together
Maintain the roster, club forms, meeting records and achievements in one place.
Reuse the roster for events
Choose the people attending instead of starting a new list each time.
See what needs attention
Directors see their next tasks. Coordinators review records and participation.
Return to the saved record
Find the report, registration, choices or approved working copy again.
slides.say: The purpose is to make ongoing club work and event work easier to connect. A director maintains the club's information. When an event opens, that roster is available for choosing who will attend. Coordinators use the same recorded work to understand progress and offer help. Returning to the saved record is more useful than keeping several different versions of a list.

slides.title: Know which job you are doing
cards: Club roster
Who belongs to the club for the year.
Event registration
Who is going to one event, and the choices made for them.
Your account
Your sign-in and the tools assigned to you.
Coordinator view
An overview of clubs, submitted records, points and participation.
slides.say: These ideas are related, but they answer different questions. Putting someone on the roster does not register that person for every event. A report being submitted does not mean an event registration is paid or checked in. Your account connects you to the responsibilities assigned to you. If you are both a director and a coordinator, choose the workspace for the task you are doing.
slides.ask: If a new member is on the roster, are they automatically registered for Honors Weekend? The answer is no.

slides.title: New director? Accept the club invitation
steps: Check the invited email
Use the address that received the invitation.
Sign in or create an account
Already have an account? Use it. New here? Create one.
Choose Accept
On your account page, accept the correct club and role.
slides.route: Your personal club invitation → Your account
slides.tip: An account and a club invitation do different jobs. Accept connects you to the club.
slides.say: The invitation is what connects your account to a club. Creating an account by itself does not complete that connection. If you already have an account at the invited address, sign in to it. If you are new, create and verify the account first. On your account page, find You're invited to manage a club, check the club name and role, and choose Accept. If the invitation is missing, ask the office to check the address rather than making another account or applying to create the club again.

slides.title: Why the extra sign-in step matters
cards: Protect the club’s records
Club tools can open personal information about young people.
Use one supported method
An authenticator app, or a passkey when offered, meets the requirement.
Keep recovery available
Save the one-time recovery codes when they are shown.
Use your own sign-in
Keep passwords and codes private; ask for your own access.
slides.say: The extra step protects club information if someone learns a password. You only need one supported method. An authenticator app generates a short code. A passkey asks your device for a fingerprint, face or PIN. The email verification code confirms the email address; the authenticator or passkey protects access to the club and coordinator tools. Saving recovery codes now can prevent a lost phone from becoming a long interruption later.

slides.title: Set up an authenticator when prompted
steps: Add the account to your app
Follow the displayed instructions and setup key.
Confirm and turn on
Enter Code from your authenticator, then confirm.
Save recovery codes

slides.say: Choose Set up an authenticator. The help link explains suitable apps, including Google Authenticator and Microsoft Authenticator. Follow the screen to add the account to your app using the setup information shown. Then enter the code from the app and choose Confirm and turn on. Save the recovery codes somewhere private and choose I've saved these codes. Continue when setup is complete. A passkey is another method if the site offers it; you do not have to set up both.

slides.title: Update a member without losing their history
cards: Edit and Save
Use the person’s Edit control to correct the existing record.
Deactivate
Keep the person on file while omitting them from new registrations.
Reactivate
Return an inactive person to the active roster when appropriate.
Remove
Read carefully: this erases roster details and cannot be undone.
slides.say: These actions have different purposes. Edit corrects the existing person. Deactivate keeps the person in your records but stops them being selected for new registrations. Show inactive lets you find that person, and Reactivate can bring them back. Remove is an erasure action. If someone may return, keeping the record is generally the useful path. Read the explanation before any removal and ask the office if you are unsure what should be retained.
slides.show: Point out the pencil/Edit action, Save and Deactivate inside the editor. If showing Remove, stop at its explanation and cancel; do not erase a real person for training.

Save the note

slides.route: Monthly Records → Month → Add meeting note
slides.tip: Meeting notes help you prepare the Monthly Record later.
slides.say: Short notes after a meeting are easier than rebuilding the whole month from memory. Open Monthly Records, choose the month and add a meeting note. Record the date and counts you know. People with roster access may also take name-by-name attendance; that is optional and is not promised to a reporter who cannot open the roster. Save the note so the information is there when you prepare the monthly report.

slides.title: Finish and submit the Monthly Record
steps: Review the month
Check the details and the due date shown.
Save draft if unfinished
A draft lets you return; it has not been submitted.
Submit report
Submit when ready and check that the result says Submitted.
slides.route: Monthly Records → Month → Open Monthly Record / Continue report
slides.tip: The current due date is the 10th of the following month. Check the date on the page.
slides.say: Saving a draft and submitting are different actions. Open or continue the Monthly Record, review its details and check the month and due date. The current rule is the tenth of the following month. Meeting notes can help fill the record. If you have already saved the report, changing a note does not silently replace that saved report; use Refresh from meeting notes deliberately if offered. Once you are ready, Submit report and confirm the submitted result. Contact the office if a closed report needs attention.

Practical orientation  ·  October 2026

YOUR CLUB

Why we use IMSDA Events
Keep club information together
Maintain the roster, club forms, meeting records and achievements in one place.

Choose the people attending instead of starting a new list each time.
See what needs attention

Who is going to one event, and the choices made for them.

Your sign-in and the tools assigned to you.

An overview of clubs, submitted records, points and participation.
